# bugs #3895: mcs51: internal error in SDCCmem.c for a 128-byte char array with an initializer

## Finding

The attachment `main.c` compiles on r17158 with the options of the ticket, `-mmcs51
--opt-code-size --fverbose-asm -c`. The compiler prints neither warning 84 nor the internal error.
The file also compiles with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, `--model-huge`, `--stack-auto`,
`--stack-auto --xstack`, and `--nooverlay`. Variants of the file compile as well: arrays of 200 and
of 300 elements, an `int` array, an `__idata` array, and a string literal as the initializer.
Linking the object file gives a regular diagnostic, which is what the first comment asks for:

    ?ASlink-Error-Could not get 128 consecutive bytes in internal RAM for area DSEG

The reporter used revision 15257 on a MinGW64 host. The tests for this entry ran on a Linux host,
and a MinGW host was not tested. The revision after which the file compiles was not identified.

Line 1292 of `src/SDCCmem.c` in r15257 is `wassert (currFunc)` in `canOverlayLocals`. The assertion
fails when the overlay segment has a symbol while no function is being compiled. The mcs51
register allocator adds such a symbol when it spills a temporary in the code that initializes a
global variable. Warning 84 in the ticket names a temporary, `iTemp254`, on the line of the array.

## Related

local 0002 has three initializers for which r17158 fails at this assertion or with a segmentation
fault in the code around it.
